clue.text: Grass boosting energy? Hardly

indicators.note: in a down clue, boosting a letter lifts it higher up the column, so it moves earlier in the word

blocks.note: barley is a cereal grass
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A lawn treated with something energising, and the question of whether the grass grew at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the E out of BARLEY and lift it one place higher in the column: BARLY becomes BAR(E)LY, BARELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely and hardly are synonymous adverbs meaning only just or scarcely.

clue.text: Game often linked with failure, initially

definitions.text: Game often linked with failure, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: opening letters of these three words
opening letter of failure

explanation.surface: A wry remark that a certain sport is usually associated with flopping.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well as builds: a game played on links, the seaside courses, spelt by the initials of the words around 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a sport played over links courses, and its frustrations make it a byword for failure.

clue.text: A smoke Dutch finds fragrant

blocks.note: per means a, as in fifty pence a go
fume is smoke or vapour
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: A Dutch smoker, or the setter Dutch himself, enjoying a pleasant-smelling cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch is also the setter's pseudonym, so the surface winks at the setter enjoying a smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfumed means scented with a pleasant smell, which is what fragrant describes.

clue.text: Hours spent working - those on a plane?

blocks.note: first meaning: the period a machine or system is running
second meaning, read whimsically: time spent up in the air

explanation.surface: A query whether hours logged by aircrew count as working time.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: hours on a plane are time spent up.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptime is the computing term for the period a system is operational and working.

clue.text: Extension for student going abroad around November

indicators.note: going abroad suggests letters wandering away from their usual order
around says the scrambled word wraps itself about another piece

blocks.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons
L is the learner driver's plate
these letters rearranged
N is November in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A student asking for an extension to study abroad over the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: N sits inside the scrambled GOING after its first letter: O(N)GING.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolonging is the act of lengthening something in time, which is an extension of it.

clue.text: Attack unexpectedly, once up and running

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly comes out in an unforeseen order

blocks.note: these letters rearranged
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A predator springing into action as soon as it is up and about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' seems to belong with Attack, and it does sharpen the sense, but it also does work scrambling the two words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pounce on someone is to spring at and seize them, a sudden assault.

clue.text: Privy Seals: a function of Charles

indicators.note: to seal something is to shut it inside, so one piece closes around the other

blocks.note: a privy is a can, American slang for a lavatory; it splits around the inner piece
taken as written
a role is a function
end of can

explanation.surface: A constitutional note on the Privy Seal as one of the king's powers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Privy Seal sounds like an office of state, but privy is a toilet, slangily a can, which seals A ROLE: C(A ROLE)AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Carolean describes things relating to King Charles I or II, from Carolus, Latin for Charles.

clue.text: Upset about courage quietly deserting, fortune not favouring one

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns a word upside down so it reads bottom to top
deserting means leaving, so that letter departs from the word

blocks.note: on means about, as in a talk on birds
pluck is courage
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone upset to find their nerve slipping away as fortune turns against them.
explanation.definitionFit: No luck is the stock phrase for an attempt where chance has not favoured one.

clue.text: A point in time

blocks.note: first meaning: the American name for a full stop
second meaning: a span of time, an era

explanation.surface: A phrase for some particular moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one idiom, but splits into a punctuation mark and a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Period is the US term for a full stop and also means an interval or era.

clue.text: Damsel fails to conceal identity

indicators.note: the phrase that conceals something holds it out of sight inside its own letters

blocks.note: runs across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A maiden in a story who cannot keep her true identity secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The self is a person's essential being, their own identity.

clue.text: Caught you blocking pitch about stuff in meeting

indicators.note: a thing blocking a gap sits inside it, so this word goes within another
about means surrounding, so the word before it wraps the word after

blocks.note: to pitch is to fling; first letter of the outer word
text-speak for you
second letter of fling
to stuff is to fill
the rest of fling

explanation.surface: An accusation that someone sabotaged a sales pitch during a business meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like a sales pitch but is the verb fling. 'Caught' only reinforces the picture of one piece trapped inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Meeting a need or demand is fulfilling it, satisfying what it requires.

clue.text: Check on limits of safety practice

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its two edges, its first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters
to stem a flow is to check it

explanation.surface: A routine of checking safety procedure at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like an inspection, but it is the verb stem, as in stemming a flow; in an across clue 'on' places it second.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is a method or established way of doing things, a practice.

clue.text: Somehow meant to run event

indicators.note: somehow says the letters get there by some unspecified rearrangement

blocks.note: these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Organisers who were supposed to stage a competition and managed it after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a sporting competition, a type of event.

clue.text: Lens care solution?

indicators.note: a solution is something worked out, so the letters before it are worked into a new order

blocks.note: these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: The fluid contact lens wearers use to keep their lenses clean.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: lens care solution is precisely a cleanser.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens care solution is a liquid that cleans lenses, so it is a cleanser.

clue.text: Reports of bastards besieging peacekeepers

indicators.note: an army besieging a town surrounds it, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: sods is British slang for unpleasant people
the United Nations sends peacekeepers

explanation.surface: News reports of thugs laying siege to a UN peacekeeping force.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports are noises, like the report of a gun, so sounds is a synonym.

clue.text: Recited passage in a normal way

indicators.note: recited means spoken out, so what matters is how the word is heard

blocks.note: a strait is a narrow sea passage

explanation.surface: A passage of text read out plainly, without dramatic flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something straight is to do it plainly and conventionally, without irony or quirks.

clue.text: The original American restaurant

blocks.note: first meaning: a Native American, the first inhabitant
second meaning: in Britain, an ... is a curry restaurant, as in going for an ...

explanation.surface: A diner boasting it was the first American-style eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage 'an Indian' means a curry house or a curry meal, so the word stands alone for the restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian is an older term for the Native peoples of the Americas and British shorthand for a curry restaurant.

clue.text: Record low after school review

indicators.note: a review looks back over something, so the word is read in the backward direction
after places the first-named piece below the second in this down entry

blocks.note: Eton, the English public school
feeling low is feeling down

explanation.surface: A school inspection report noting a poor showing.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is England's best-known private boarding school; in this down clue 'low after' it puts DOWN below it.
explanation.definitionFit: To note down is to write something to record it.

clue.text: One woman's husband falling for another

indicators.note: in a down clue, falling means sinking lower in the column, so that letter moves later

blocks.note: Hester is a woman's name
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife leaving her husband for another person.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a husband falling for another woman; really, the H in HESTER drops down three places to give another woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a female name, so it is another woman alongside the first one.

clue.text: Leaving city, Eccles packs a lot of ice for twists

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the city's letters go out of the town's name
to pack something is to put it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
Eccles is a town near Manchester
a rink is a big sheet of ice

explanation.surface: A Mancunian town's ice packing comes out twisted, oddly worded like a weather report.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles is a town near Manchester, known for its currant cakes; the City of London's postcode is the conventional source of the city's two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Crinkles are small folds or twists in a surface such as paper or skin.

clue.text: Permissive landlord?

blocks.note: surface reading: an easygoing owner who allows tenants anything
setter's reading: one who lets, both permitting things and renting out property

explanation.walkthrough: Let means both allow and rent out, so a one-who-lets word covers both halves of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter, besides a written message, is someone who lets property, or simply allows things.

clue.text: Clothing scraps less feminine after time?

indicators.note: less means minus, so the stated letter is subtracted

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
scraps are scuffles or fights
F is the abbreviation for feminine

explanation.surface: Old clothes being cut down to look less girly after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scraps' looks like offcuts of cloth, but means fights.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights are a close-fitting legwear garment, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Secure remuneration for speech in capital

indicators.note: for speech means the words are to be heard spoken, not read

blocks.note: to tie is to secure; pay is remuneration

explanation.surface: Negotiating a speaking fee for an address in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Taipei is the capital city of Taiwan.

clue.text: Clashing as mad chemist dispensed liberally

indicators.note: something dispensed liberally is handed out freely and scattered about

blocks.note: these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A deranged pharmacist handing out drugs freely, causing chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Mismatched things do not go together, so they clash.

clue.text: Train app used regularly when heading west to find partner

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept
in an across clue, heading west means travelling right to left

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Using a rail app for a westbound trip to meet one's other half.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a couple, and to partner someone is to pair with them; here as a noun, one's other half.

clue.text: Marquis de Sade obviously enjoyed this offering from the boulangerie

definitions.text: Marquis de Sade obviously enjoyed this

blocks.clueFragment: Marquis de Sade obviously enjoyed this
blocks.note: first meaning: suffering, which the famous sadist relished
second meaning: the French word for bread, sold at a French bakery

explanation.walkthrough: The French setting of both halves makes it look like one Gallic idea, but one is English and one is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain is suffering in English, which a sadist enjoys, and bread in French, which a baker sells.

clue.text: Cash put up will be invested in church

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so this piece goes inside

blocks.note: CE, the Church of England; first letter
to put up a picture is to hang it
second letter of CE

explanation.surface: Donations given to a church to be invested by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Change is cash in coins, the loose money in one's pocket.

clue.text: Alterations extended, ignoring German customs

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: grew means extended or increased
G is the abbreviation for German
rites are customary ceremonies

explanation.surface: Changes stretching out because German customs procedures were skipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs' suggests border control but means traditional rites.
explanation.definitionFit: Rewrites are revised versions of a text, i.e. alterations made to it.
